To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel GAN architecture, OT-GAN, that combines a new metric, mini-batch energy distances, and optimal transport in primal and dual form to train generative models.

(1) OT-GAN is the first GAN to be stable when trained with mini-batches, (2) the energy distance metric is an unbiased estimator of the true Wasserstein distance and thus is a good choice in practice, and (3) the mini-batch energy loss function is a highly discriminative criterion for evaluating generative models.

we propose a new metric, mini-batch energy, that combines optimal transport with adversarially learned features, and that we show that this metric improves the training stability of generative adversarials nets.

developing new methods for GAN training, and in particular we propose a new distance function for GANs based on optimal transport.
improving the stability and performance of GANs, and we achieve this goal by using a new GAN metric based on optimal transport.
developing new methods for training generative models, which are capable of producing high quality synthetic images.

the OT-GAN achieves a new state-of-the-art in terms of image quality and model stability when trained with large batch sizes, and is well suited for high-dimensional and large-scale data sets.
the OT-GAN is the most promising GAN method at present.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce an algorithm for generating high dimensional discrete data, which is a new type of GAN.
we present OT-GAN, a new GAN model that achieves state of the art results using a novel optimal transport distance metric, mini-batch energy distances.
the mini-batch energy-distance, which we propose to call the Wasserstein distance, is a stable, efficient, and unbiased metric that is well suited for generative modeling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
optimal transport is a natural choice for a GAN distance function, with a simple and intuitive interpretation as an average difference between probability distributions.

optimal transport, when used in combination with a GAN, is a simple yet powerful idea that results in a stable training procedure, better sample quality and an unbiased estimator of the Wasserstein distance between distributions.

the mini-batch energy distances are a generalization of the Wasserstein distance that can be used to stabilize GANs with large mini-batch sizes, and we show that the mini-batches do not need to be sampled from the same distribution.
